items.en: Kuzu (arrowroot) Mochi with Tanba Black Soybeans
items.note: Shop states kuzu starch with lightly-simmered Tanba black soybeans — no wheat in the wrapper, but the simmering liquid for the beans is not disclosed and Japanese black-bean nimame often includes soy sauce; the same counter handles fu-manju (wheat gluten) and kuri-manju (wheat). Price is the 6-piece gift box.

items.ja: 丹波黒豆入り抹茶くず餅
items.en: Matcha Kuzu Mochi with Tanba Black Soybeans
items.note: Matcha version of the kuzu mochi; same caveat — bean simmering liquid undisclosed, wheat items handled in the same shop. 6-piece gift box.
MUSHI-yokan (steamed), not neri-yokan — steamed yokan is traditionally bound with WHEAT FLOUR (some makers use kuzu instead). The shop does not state which. Do not treat as GF without asking.
Seasonal. Same wheat-flour binder risk as the plain steamed chestnut yokan — confirm before eating.

Warabi/starch jelly with matcha; no wheat by composition. Usually dusted with kinako (roasted soybean flour) which is also wheat-free. Shared wagashi counter also handles wheat sweets — ask them to cut and serve away from the fu-manju.

items.section: 和菓子 (Wagashi) · 初秋〜春・実演販売のみ
items.note: Manju dough is wheat flour — not gluten-free. Baked manju is commonly egg-glazed; confirm for vegan. Sold only at the in-store demonstration counter, early autumn to spring.

Shop states: Tanba Sasayama black soybeans simmered lightly, the simmering liquid finished with Amami kokuto (brown sugar). No wheat ingredient named, but the bean simmering liquid may contain soy sauce, and the gelling agent (agar vs gelatin) is not stated — ask on both counts.
Mizu-yokan is set with agar (kanten), not flour — unlike the steamed mushi-yokan above. Red bean paste and sugar only. Summer item.
Ginger de-bittered and candied in sugar; shop lists no other ingredient. No price posted on the shop's site.
The shop states the wrapper is 生麩 (nama-fu — raw WHEAT GLUTEN) with yomogi, filled with tsubu-an. This is pure gluten; absolutely not for celiacs. Plant ingredients only, so vegan.

Sold as 丹波黒豆葛まんじゅう / くずまんじゅう. Kuzu-starch wrapper around bean paste — wheat-free by composition, unlike the wheat-flour kuri-manju and the wheat-gluten fu-manju sold beside it. Ask staff to handle it separately.

items.en: Ohagi (Glutinous Rice Ball with Bean Paste)
items.section: 和菓子 (Wagashi) · 春〜秋・店頭販売のみ
items.note: Glutinous rice with azuki paste or kinako — no wheat. 'Glutinous' here means sticky rice, not gluten. In-store sale only.

items.section: 和菓子 (Wagashi) · 初春〜春・店頭販売のみ
items.note: House-named spring confection; the shop publishes no ingredients for it. Unknown base — must ask whether it is rice-, kuzu- or wheat-based.

items.section: 和菓子 (Wagashi) · 初春〜春・店頭販売のみ
items.note: In Kansai sakuramochi is normally the Domyoji style (coarse glutinous rice = wheat-free), but the Kanto style uses a WHEAT-FLOUR crepe. The shop does not say which it makes — ask for 道明寺 (domyoji).

items.section: 和菓子 (Wagashi) · 初春〜春・店頭販売のみ
items.note: Pounded glutinous rice with mugwort and bean paste — no wheat. Note the shop's fu-manju also uses yomogi but is wheat gluten; make sure you are handed the mochi, not the fu-manju.

items.section: 和菓子 (Wagashi) · 節句限定・店頭販売のみ
items.note: Non-glutinous rice-flour dough with bean paste, wrapped in an oak leaf — wheat-free. Boys'-Day season only, in-store.

items.section: 丹波黒豆 (Tanba Black Soybean products)
items.note: 330g. Shop says only 'simmered lightly'. Japanese kuromame nimame is very often simmered with soy sauce (wheat) for colour — ask before eating. Plant-only otherwise.

items.section: 丹波黒豆 (Tanba Black Soybean products)
items.note: Dry-roasted beans, no seasoning described — wheat-free and plant-only. Shop's site marks this 只今販売停止中 (sales currently suspended) and posts no price.

items.section: 丹波黒豆 (Tanba Black Soybean products)
items.note: 100g. Made by drying the simmered beans, so it carries the same undisclosed-simmering-liquid soy-sauce question as the nimame.

items.section: 丹波黒豆 (Tanba Black Soybean products)
items.note: Roasted black soybeans milled to powder — soy flour, no wheat. Shop's site marks this 只今販売停止中 (sales currently suspended) and posts no price.

items.section: 丹波黒豆 (Tanba Black Soybean products)
items.note: 1 bag. Roasted black soybean pieces brewed as tea — single ingredient, no wheat, no animal products. Also the safest thing in the shop for a celiac.

items.section: 詰め合わせ (Gift sets) · 季節限定
items.note: Mixed gift box — contents vary by season and can include the wheat-gluten fu-manju and wheat-flour kuri-manju. Ask for the contents list before buying; no price posted.

items.ja: チキンカレー（3種の鶏のチキンカレー）
items.romaji: Chicken Curry (3-shu no Tori no Chicken Curry)
items.note: Signature dish. Built from 10+ whole spices and 10kg/day of slow-fried Awaji onions — no wheat roux, which is the usual gluten source in Japanese curry. But no GF claim is made anywhere and soy sauce in the base is unconfirmed. Contains chicken.

items.ja: 海老のグリーンカレー（海老と野菜のグリーンカレー）
items.note: Thai-leaning: prawn-shell stock, coconut milk, green chilli, kaffir lime leaf, with daikon/carrot/bamboo shoot. Green curry paste commonly contains shrimp paste and sometimes fish sauce — no GF claim. Contains shellfish.

items.ja: 厚あげの豆カレー（厚揚げと小松菜の豆カレー）
items.note: THE dish to order here if you are vegan. Two independent food outlets report the shop created it for vegan and allergy-restricted visitors and that it uses no animal ingredients at all — chana dal with cubed atsuage and Nepali sansho. Still confirm on the day (the shop makes no published claim itself), and it is not a GF claim: soy sauce and the atsuage's frying oil are unaccounted for.

items.ja: あいがけ（コンビネーション）
items.note: Choose two of the three standard curries on one plate, salad included. Pick the bean curry twice / with a vegan daily special if you need it plant-based — the plates touch. Reported at ¥1,300–¥1,600 across 2023–2026 write-ups; ¥1,600 is the most recent figure.

All three curries plus keema, house spice chicken ham, papad, chicken skin and sambol on one plate. Contains chicken and — via the green curry — shellfish. Papad and the ham make the gluten picture worse, not better; ask item by item.

items.section: カレー (Curry) · 気まぐれ/日替わり
items.note: Appears as a topping on the Special and as an irregular daily curry (a mackerel keema has been served). Deliberately kept mild, so a kids' plate can sometimes be made from it. Meat or fish; no price posted.

items.section: カレー (Curry) · 気まぐれ/日替わり
items.note: An unlisted fourth curry appears some days (Indian, Sri Lankan, Thai or Japanese-leaning) and can be combined in the aigake. Because it is unlisted, nothing about its ingredients is knowable in advance — ask before ordering it.

items.ja: 自家製スパイス鶏ハム
items.note: Cured chicken breast. Cures and brines routinely include soy sauce; unconfirmed here. Contains chicken.

items.ja: トロトロ溶かしチーズ
items.note: Dairy cheese — vegetarian but not vegan. Plain melted cheese carries no wheat.

items.section: トッピング (Toppings) · スペシャル付属
items.note: Indian lentil-flour cracker. Usually chickpea/urad flour and wheat-free, but many commercial papads add wheat flour or asafoetida cut with wheat, and it is normally flash-fried in shared oil. Comes on the Suehiro Special. No separate price posted.

items.section: トッピング (Toppings) · スペシャル付属
items.note: Sri Lankan coconut relish served on the Special. Classic pol sambol is coconut, chilli, onion and lime — but Maldive fish (dried tuna) is the traditional inclusion, so ask before treating it as vegan.

items.section: サイド (Sides) · 播州テイスト
items.note: Local Banshu grilled mature-hen dish dressed in ponzu. Ponzu is soy-sauce based (wheat) and the dish is chicken — bad on both counts. Appears as a Banshu accent, notably on the Special.
Soy-milk lassi — the dairy-free drink option here. Confirm no yoghurt or honey is blended in before calling it vegan.
Two whole bananas per glass, blended with dairy milk. ¥100 off when ordered with a curry.
Dairy milk blend. ¥100 off with a curry order.
The owner states a kids' plate is available; it is usually built from the mild keema and may need to be requested/discussed in advance. Contents therefore vary — ask.

items.ja: おやさいたっぷり日替わりランチ
items.note: The one main thing this kitchen serves: a main you pick (meat or fish), four vegetable side dishes, salad, clear soup, rice and dessert. THE key fact for vegans — the house dashi is shiitake and kombu only, with katsuobushi and saba-bushi deliberately excluded so a vegan order can always be filled. Say vegan or vegetarian when you order and the owner rebuilds the plate. Gluten is the unresolved half: soy sauce, miso and mirin run through the sides and no tamari is documented.

items.ja: 豆腐ステーキ（ヴィーガン対応メイン）
items.en: Tofu Steak — the standard vegan main
items.section: ランチ (Lunch) · ヴィーガン対応
items.note: The default main swapped in for vegan diners. Glazed in a house sauce reduced from sugar, SOY SAUCE and mirin with ginger — standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat and no tamari substitution is documented, so this is a vegan dish that is NOT safe for celiacs unless they change the glaze. Ask for it plain/unglazed. Priced within the daily lunch set.

items.ja: ヴィーガン対応プレート
items.section: ランチ (Lunch) · ヴィーガン対応
items.note: The owner builds a plate with no animal ingredients at all on request — the plant dashi makes this genuine rather than approximate. Best to phone ahead. Still ask separately about wheat: the vegan adaptation addresses animal products, not gluten.

items.ja: ベジタリアン対応プレート
items.section: ランチ (Lunch) · ベジタリアン対応
items.note: For lacto-ovo vegetarians the owner adds egg and dairy as wanted; she asks about spice tolerance too. By definition contains egg/dairy.

Rotating: reported examples include onishime (simmered vegetables), amamiso-itame (sweet-miso stir-fry), su-zuke (vinegar pickles), simmered koyadofu and sweet-simmered daikon. Plant dashi throughout, so usually vegan-adaptable — but the miso and simmering seasonings are the gluten problem. Miso is often barley or wheat-containing; ask which they use.
Named example of the sides. Koyadofu itself is only soybean, and the dashi here is shiitake/kombu, so it is vegan — but it is simmered in seasoning that almost certainly includes soy sauce. Ask.
Deliberately sweetened so it does not taste like the other simmered dishes. Vegan thanks to the plant dashi; soy sauce in the simmering liquid unconfirmed.

Shiitake/kombu dashi with a tofu flower floating in it — vegan, and one of the few Japanese clear soups you can trust on the dashi question. Suimono is normally seasoned with usukuchi soy sauce, so still ask for GF.
Plain steamed rice with the set — unseasoned, so it is the reliable base of the meal for a celiac. Confirm it is not takikomi (seasoned) rice on the day.

items.ja: やさいの手作りシフォンケーキ
items.note: The house signature — pumpkin, carrot, molokheiya, black soybean and 10+ other rotating flavours. Explicitly made with DOMESTIC WHEAT FLOUR and beet sugar, no baking powder and no artificial colour or MSG. Wheat flour makes it categorically off-limits for celiacs, and a chiffon raised without baking powder depends on whipped egg — not vegan.

items.ja: 食後のドリンクとシフォンケーキ
items.romaji: Shokugo no Drink to Chiffon Cake
items.note: +¥200 on the daily lunch. Skip the add-on if you are avoiding wheat or egg — the cake is the whole point of it. Drink choice is hot coffee or tea.

items.ja: ケーキセット（ドリンク付き）
items.note: Cafe-time set built on the wheat-flour chiffon cake. Same wheat and egg problem as the cake itself.

items.ja: 新鮮フルーツのミックスジュース
items.section: ドリンク (Drinks) · スペシャルドリンクセット
items.note: Made from the fruit on the greengrocer stand out front — the husband wholesales produce at Himeji central market. Kansai mix juice conventionally includes milk, so confirm for vegan. Part of the Special Drink Set.

items.ja: おまかせランチ（obann・水〜土）
items.note: SHARE CAFE — a different independent vendor cooks each weekday in this renovated 1890s Tanabiki Seimen head office, so there is no standing menu, no shared allergen policy and no single kitchen to hold accountable. Check the venue Instagram for who is cooking before you go and ask that vendor directly. Closed Sundays. The nearest thing Eni has to a regular menu: obann took the Wed–Sat slot and serves a vegetable-forward obanzai plate. Obanzai is soy-sauce, miso and dashi cooking by definition, so assume wheat in the seasoning and bonito in the dashi until this vendor tells you otherwise. Building context: landlord Tanabiki Seimen makes Banryu somen, Banryu soba (wheat-blended, not juwari) and Banryutei udon, but states these are sold online only and NOT in this building — the cafe is a renovated office, not the noodle plant.

items.en: Bento Box — vendor 'obann', reserve by the day before
items.note: SHARE CAFE — a different independent vendor cooks each weekday in this renovated 1890s Tanabiki Seimen head office, so there is no standing menu, no shared allergen policy and no single kitchen to hold accountable. Check the venue Instagram for who is cooking before you go and ask that vendor directly. Closed Sundays. From ¥1,000, reservation required by the previous day. Reserving is the opening to state dietary needs in advance — the one genuine advantage of ordering here.

items.ja: 週替りランチ（2nd Kitchen HINATA・月火）
items.en: Weekly-Changing Teishoku Lunch — vendor '2nd Kitchen HINATA', Mon & Tue
items.note: SHARE CAFE — a different independent vendor cooks each weekday in this renovated 1890s Tanabiki Seimen head office, so there is no standing menu, no shared allergen policy and no single kitchen to hold accountable. Check the venue Instagram for who is cooking before you go and ask that vendor directly. Closed Sundays. Drink included. Japanese teishoku format: one main, two or three seasonal vegetable kobachi, goma-dofu, soup and rice. Goma-dofu is sesame set with kuzu starch, so it is normally wheat-free and plant-based — but the soup and kobachi are dashi and soy-sauce territory. Run by one person alone; limited daily covers and she may turn people away.

SHARE CAFE — a different independent vendor cooks each weekday in this renovated 1890s Tanabiki Seimen head office, so there is no standing menu, no shared allergen policy and no single kitchen to hold accountable. Check the venue Instagram for who is cooking before you go and ask that vendor directly. Closed Sundays. +¥300 on the weekly lunch; a separate cafe dessert menu also exists for non-lunch visits. Contents change weekly and are unpublished — ask.

SHARE CAFE — a different independent vendor cooks each weekday in this renovated 1890s Tanabiki Seimen head office, so there is no standing menu, no shared allergen policy and no single kitchen to hold accountable. Check the venue Instagram for who is cooking before you go and ask that vendor directly. Closed Sundays. Sold by the piece for takeaway, no reservation needed. Because they are made and sold individually you can ask about each one — the most workable option here for a restricted diet. No fixed prices published.
